name: Woodrow H. Levin
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Extend (product-protection / extended-warranty platform for merchants)
profile: Serial founder Woody Levin co-founded Extend, a San Francisco platform that lets merchants sell product-protection plans online; it raised a $260M SoftBank-led Series C in 2021 at a $1.6B+ valuation. Earlier he founded gaming company BringIt (sold to IGT in 2012), stadium-ad firm InStadium and Estate Assist.
interesting_fact: He pitched Extend directly to SoftBank's Masayoshi Son, who he said 'immediately understood what we were doing'; his stated goal is to be the 'AppleCare' for everything that isn't an Apple product.
deep_cut_fact: Before Extend he founded InStadium, the NFL advertising company behind the ads in stadium bathrooms ('his idea'), and started Estate Assist (digital-asset estate planning) after watching his family of lawyers scramble for his grandmother's information after she died.

public_contacts.value: Danielle Vaknin, ASTRSK PR - extend@astrskpr.com (Extend media contact, Jan 2022 release)

notes: PR contact is from a 2022 release and may be stale. Search results also say he sits on the DraftKings board, but I could not open the DraftKings IR page to confirm it.

name: Aaron King
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Snapdocs (CEO until Sept 2023)
profile: Aaron King founded Snapdocs in 2013. It started as a mobile-notary scheduling tool and grew into a digital mortgage-closing platform valued at about $2B. He led it as CEO for a decade, then handed the CEO role to Michael Sachdev in Sept 2023 and stayed on full-time as executive chairman, focused on product direction and customers.
interesting_fact: He was a mortgage-industry veteran of roughly 20 years who worked as a notary signing agent himself. That front-line experience led to a nationwide notary signing service and eventually Snapdocs.
deep_cut_fact: Asked for the best advice he ever received, he said: 'There's tremendous power in being a great listener... hyper-effective leaders continuously hone this skill.'

public_contacts.value: Sam Garcia, Strategic Vantage Marketing & PR - samgarcia@strategicvantage.com

notes: Aggregator sites say his earlier notary company was NotaryLink, founded at age 21; I could not confirm this from a primary source. Contacts come from a Sept 2023 release.

name: Ziv Paz
current_role: Co-founder (non-operational) of Melio (former COO); current venture not verified
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Melio, a B2B payments platform for small businesses, in 2018 with Matan Bar and Ilan Atias. As COO and the company's number two he led operations and go-to-market. He gave up his operational role in 2021. Xero agreed in 2025 to buy Melio for up to $3B, and CTech reported that each co-founder holds about 9%.
interesting_fact: He was the only Melio founder without a technology background. He studied law and accounting after long service in the IDF naval commando unit Shayetet 13.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 2.5 years as a VP at FIMI Opportunity Funds and was on track to run a portfolio company and return as a partner. He left instead to start Melio with Matan Bar, his childhood school friend from Haifa.
notes: Left his operational role at Melio in 2021 (https://www.calcalistech.com/ctech/articles/0,7340,L-3923561,00.html). Melio is now part of Xero. An aggregator says he started a new company in 2024; I could not verify this. No published contact found; LinkedIn is likely the best route.
